user_story: As a user, I want the app to estimate my remaining time from my birth date and model inputs so the countdown is deterministic and inspectable.
expected_behavior: A valid birth date produces a valid estimate with age, death date, remaining milliseconds, progress from 0 to 1, and one of calm/finite/near/borrowed states. Invalid dates return an invalid estimate without crashing.
notes: Uses population life expectancy as a reflective model, not an individual prediction.

user_story: As a user who moved countries, I want birth country, current country, and move age to influence the model without pretending to be clinical.
expected_behavior: Different birth/current countries blend toward the current residence after move age; no blend is applied before move age or when countries match.
notes: Model intentionally coarse; city-level effects are out of scope.

user_story: As a user, I want simple checkbox rows for sex, sleep, exercise, drinking, smoking, and health so I can make the model less generic.
expected_behavior: Each factor behaves as a mutually exclusive row, unchecked rows are skipped internally, and selected values change life expectancy by documented local offsets.
notes: No dropdowns for custom settings.

user_story: As a user, I want every main countdown surface to include seconds so the widget feels alive and precise enough for the concept.
expected_behavior: Full readouts include years, days, hours, minutes, and seconds; borrowed time is prefixed with plus.
notes: The product still labels estimates as approximate.

user_story: As a Linux bar user, I want a tiny JSON emitter so Waybar can display the countdown with classes, tooltip, and progress.
expected_behavior: Emitter loads a config or sample defaults, outputs compact JSON with text, tooltip, class array, and percentage, and includes the full disclaimer in tooltip/sample config.
notes: Linux/Waybar remains the reference implementation.

user_story: As a product reviewer, I want Linux, macOS, and W11 tray previews so the primary widget can be compared across OS conventions.
expected_behavior: Local app shows Linux system tray, macOS status menu bar, and W11 system tray with only the MM widget and system clock, with progress integrated in the widget.
notes: No adjacent fake shell items such as Finder, Start, Search, or Activities.

user_story: As a user, I want one right-click menu action to toggle between bone/ash and onyx palettes without nested settings.
expected_behavior: All three preview menus plus the live context menu expose one palette toggle; toggling updates the document skin and all palette buttons consistently.
notes: Visible labels remain bone and ash / onyx; internal skin IDs stay system-light/system-dark.

user_story: As a user, I want the full panel to minimize back into the tray widget and restore on double click so the app behaves like a tray utility.
expected_behavior: Clicking Minimize hides the panel and shows the dock widget; double-clicking the dock widget restores the panel; double-clicking panel chrome minimizes unless editing controls are targeted.
notes: Settings live inside the maximized panel.

user_story: As a non-technical user, I want one visible setup panel with no tabs or generated backend config so changing inputs recalculates immediately.
expected_behavior: Birth date, birth country, living country, since age, and checkbox rows are visible in one panel; edits update countdown/death date/model age without a restart button.
notes: Quickstart/custom split and restart clock remain removed.

user_story: As a user, I want occasional dry reminders that time is finite without titles or medical shame.
expected_behavior: Reflection copy has no popup title, uses gently acidic prompts, adapts late-night pool for late hours, and renders at minimized widget width.
notes: Tone is dry, not cruel.

user_story: As a buyer/reviewer, I want the UI to feel stylish and specific rather than generic boilerplate.
expected_behavior: Local app uses bone/ash and onyx/gold palettes, hourglass/bone/candle motifs, Fraunces for display moments, Geist for UI, and system fallbacks.
notes: External font loading is progressive enhancement; fallbacks remain defined.

feature: Desktop and mobile app surface previews
user_story: As a product reviewer, I want Linux, Windows, macOS, and iOS app/widget previews so native direction stays visually coherent.
expected_behavior: The component app shows desktop app previews for Linux, Windows 11, macOS, and iOS icon/widget shapes that reuse the same mark, widget text, progress, reflection copy, and palette variables.
notes: These are component previews; production native wrappers must follow the release gate.

user_story: As a maintainer, I want the local app to load reliably so design and behavior checks do not depend on fragile browser defaults.
expected_behavior: npm run serve uses the Node static server, binds to 127.0.0.1, exposes /__health, disables cache, and serves explicit HTML/CSS/JS content types.
notes: Avoids ES module loading issues from direct file URLs.

user_story: As a user, I want clear install paths for release artifacts and source builds so I can run the product on my own machines.
expected_behavior: Docs identify Linux source/Waybar as the reference path and describe release-artifact/source paths for Linux, macOS, Windows 11, and iOS.
notes: No support entitlement; Apache-2.0 source remains forkable.

user_story: As a desktop user, I want source installers that create a local launcher without hiding what is being installed.
expected_behavior: macOS installer creates an app bundle that runs the local server; Windows installer creates a Start Menu shortcut that runs the local server; uninstall scripts remove those launcher files.
notes: Source installers are not described as signed native installers.

user_story: As a release user, I want packaged artifacts with checksums and a manifest so I can inspect exactly what is being distributed.
expected_behavior: Packaging builds Linux Waybar and local-app tarballs, writes SHA256SUMS, writes release-manifest.json, and includes the docs/scripts needed to reproduce the release gate.
notes: The manifest records platform readiness and the release gate honestly.

user_story: As a privacy-conscious user, I want the profile and countdown to stay local so mortality cosplay does not become telemetry.
expected_behavior: The app stores profile data in browser local storage for the local app, uses local config files for Waybar, exposes only a local development server, and documents that payment is separate from runtime countdown data.
notes: No analytics, accounts, cloud sync, or runtime countdown API are part of the current product.

user_story: As a reader, I want the philosophical justification and safety boundaries documented so the product tone is coherent and not irresponsible.
expected_behavior: README links philosophy; docs explain memento mori purpose, dry tone boundaries, classical motifs, approximate model status, and open-source commercial posture.
notes: The joke targets procrastination/self-deception, not illness or mortality itself.

user_story: As a buyer, I want to understand the difference between free source and paid convenience installers before paying.
expected_behavior: Docs state the Apache-2.0 source remains free and forkable, paid Stripe checkout sells packaging convenience, no support entitlement is implied, and beehiiv/personal-site distribution can point to GitHub Releases.
notes: Payment must never gate the source code or imply medical accuracy.

user_story: As a maintainer, I want one canonical spreadsheet of user stories and status so feature drift has somewhere obvious to die quietly.
expected_behavior: docs/feature-status.csv contains one row per current product or release feature, includes expected behavior, source refs, test refs, latest result, errors found, retest result, and is validated by automated tests.
notes: CSV remains the single canonical spreadsheet because it is reviewable in git and opens in spreadsheet tools.

user_story: As a release owner, I want signed installer requirements documented so source-installable builds are not oversold as finished native distribution.
expected_behavior: Native packaging docs define macOS Developer ID/notarization/stapling, Windows Authenticode/SmartScreen expectations, iOS TestFlight/App Store privacy requirements, and the rule that unsigned source installers stay labeled source-installable.
notes: This is a release-readiness feature; it prevents marketing language from outrunning the artifacts.

user_story: As a release owner, I want production scope tracked in a machine-checkable matrix so the release can be shipped honestly without hand-wavy confidence.
expected_behavior: production-readiness.json lists functional, documentation, platform, privacy, release, QA, UI, and GitHub hygiene requirements with evidence files; npm run check:production validates the matrix and npm run verify executes it.
notes: The release is production-scoped as source-installable, not as a signed native-installer release.
